name: Pale Laelia Pink
lede: Pale Laelia Pink is a soft, dusty rose, built by putting the modifier pale in front of the base color [[laelia-pink]], named for the laelia orchid's own pink.

sections.title: A modifier on an orchid's name
sections.body:
Pale Laelia Pink puts the modifier word pale in front of the base color [[laelia-pink]], in the compound-modifier grammar our library uses for names like this one, with the base name pointing to *Laelia*, a genus of showy pink and purple orchids [1]. Robert Ridgway first listed this swatch in his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, plate XXXVIII, hue 67, tone f, and the Inter-Society Color Council later filed it in the ISCC-NBS 1955 system as block 249 (R) [1]. The library also flags it as a near-duplicate of a separate Ridgway and ISCC-NBS entry, Pale Vinaceous, only 2.5 units away [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[light-pinkish-lilac]], 3.2 units off, close enough on screen to read as the same dusty pink [2]; [[queen-pink]] sits 4.0 units away, lighter and purpler [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in just 27 of 23,781 paintings, 0.11 percent, as photographed; looking for real coverage inside each painting narrows that to 18, rarer than 62 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. It most often plays a light, in 44 percent of its 18 appearances by lightness rank, so varnish cannot fake the result [3].

The earliest match dates to 1452, a painting by Bartolomeo Caporali, 460 years before Ridgway's 1912 plate [3]. That is a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin; it marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment or orchid petal [3].
